title: KCET 2009 Physics
subject: physics
source: KEA question paper (copy) + KEA answer key column A1

questions.q: The number of significant figures in the numbers $4.8000 \times 10^4$ and $48000.50$ are respectively
questions.explanation: $4.8000\times10^4$ has 5 significant figures; $48000.50$ has 7 (all digits count since the decimal point fixes the trailing zeros as significant).

questions.q: β-decay means emission of electron from
questions.explanation: In β-decay a neutron inside an unstable (radioactive) nucleus converts to a proton, emitting an electron (and antineutrino) from the nucleus itself.

questions.q: An electric heater rated 220 V and 550 W is connected to A.C. mains. The current drawn by it is

A body of mass 'm' moving along a straight line covers half the distance with a speed of $2\ \text{ms}^{-1}$. The remaining half of the distance is covered in two equal time intervals with a speed of $3\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ and $5\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ respectively. The average speed of the particle for the entire journey is
questions.explanation: For distance $d$: time for first half $= d/4$; if each equal time interval is $T$, $3T+5T=d/2 \Rightarrow T=d/16$; total time $=3d/8$, so average speed $= d/(3d/8) = 8/3\ \text{ms}^{-1}$.

questions.q: The moment of inertia of a circular ring of radius 'r' and mass 'M' about diameter is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: By the perpendicular axis theorem, $I_{diameter} = \dfrac{1}{2}I_{axis} = \dfrac{1}{2}Mr^2$.

questions.q: A body of mass 0.05 kg is observed to fall with an acceleration of $9.5\ \text{ms}^{-2}$. The opposing force of air on the body is ______ ($g = 9.8\ \text{ms}^{-2}$).
questions.explanation: Net force $= m(g-a) = 0.05\times(9.8-9.5) = 0.05\times0.3 = 0.015\ \text{N}$, which is the air resistance opposing the fall.

questions.q: The colloidal solution in which both the dispersed phase and dispersion medium are liquids called
questions.explanation: A colloidal system with a liquid dispersed phase in a liquid dispersion medium (e.g. milk) is called an emulsion. [Note: this question tests a chemistry topic printed in this physics booklet; the KEA physics key confirms this answer for Q7.]

questions.q: In fog, photographs of the objects taken with infra-red radiations are more clear than those obtained during visible light because
options: scattering of I-R light is more than visible light
the intensity of I-R light from the object is less
scattering of I-R light is less than visible light
I-R radiation has lesser wavelength than visible radiation
questions.explanation: Scattering intensity varies as $1/\lambda^4$ (Rayleigh scattering); since infrared has a longer wavelength than visible light, it scatters less in fog, giving clearer images.

questions.q: Three concurrent co-planar forces 1 N, 2 N and 3 N acting along different directions on a body
options: can keep the body in equilibrium if 1 N and 2 N act at right angles.
cannot keep the body in equilibrium.
can keep the body in equilibrium if 1 N and 3 N act at an acute angle.
can keep the body in equilibrium if 2 N and 3 N act at right angles.
questions.explanation: The maximum possible resultant of the 1 N and 2 N forces is 3 N, and only when they are collinear (0° apart) — at any other angle (right angle, acute angle, etc.) their resultant is less than 3 N and can never balance the 3 N force, so equilibrium is impossible.

questions.q: Sound waves transfer
questions.explanation: A sound wave carries energy from source to receiver and also transfers momentum (which is why sound can exert radiation pressure).

questions.q: Two rectangular blocks A and B of masses 2 kg and 3 kg respectively are connected by a spring of spring constant $10.8\ \text{Nm}^{-1}$ are placed on a frictionless horizontal surface. The block 'A' was given an initial velocity of $0.15\ \text{ms}^{-1}$ [towards B]. The maximum compression of the spring during the motion is
questions.explanation: Maximum compression occurs at common velocity $v'=\dfrac{2\times0.15}{5}=0.06\ \text{ms}^{-1}$. Energy stored $=\dfrac{1}{2}(2)(0.15)^2-\dfrac{1}{2}(5)(0.06)^2=0.0225-0.009=0.0135\ \text{J}=\dfrac{1}{2}kx^2 \Rightarrow x=0.05\ \text{m}$.

questions.q: G.P. Thomson experimentally confirmed the existence of matter waves by the phenomena
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: G.P. Thomson observed electron diffraction rings from a thin metal foil, confirming the wave nature of electrons (de Broglie waves).

questions.q: The resistance of a wire at 300 K is found to be $0.3\ \Omega$. If the temperature co-efficient of resistance of wire is $1.5\times10^{-3}\ \text{K}^{-1}$, the temperature at which the resistance becomes $0.6\ \Omega$ is
questions.explanation: Using $R_T=R_0[1+\alpha(T-T_0)]$: $2=1+1.5\times10^{-3}\Delta T \Rightarrow \Delta T \approx 667\ \text{K}$, giving $T\approx967\ \text{K}$ (closest option, 993 K, as per KEA key).

questions.q: The work done by a force acting on a body is as shown in the graph [F(N) vs S(m): F rises linearly from 0 to 10 N as S goes 0 to 5 m, stays constant at 10 N from S=5 to 15 m, then rises linearly from 10 N to 20 N as S goes from 15 to 20 m]. The total work done in covering an initial distance of 20 m is
questions.explanation: Work = area under F-S graph = triangle (0-5m): $\tfrac{1}{2}\times5\times10=25$ J, rectangle (5-15m): $10\times10=100$ J, trapezium (15-20m): $\tfrac{1}{2}(10+20)\times5=75$ J; total $=25+100+75=200$ J.

questions.q: Two luminous point sources separated by a certain distance are at 10 km from an observer. If the aperture of his eye is $2.5\times10^{-3}$ m and the wavelength of light used is 500 nm, the distance of separation between the point sources are just seen to be resolved is
questions.explanation: By Rayleigh's criterion, separation $x=\dfrac{1.22\lambda D}{a}=\dfrac{1.22\times500\times10^{-9}\times10^4}{2.5\times10^{-3}}=2.44\ \text{m}$.

questions.q: A door of 1.6 m wide requires a force of 1 N to be applied at the free end to open or close it. The force that is required at a point 0.4 m distant from the hinges for opening or closing the door is
questions.chapter: System of Particles and Rotational Motion
questions.explanation: Torque is constant: $1\times1.6 = F\times0.4 \Rightarrow F=4\ \text{N}$.

questions.q: $0.1\ \text{m}^3$ of water at 80 °C is mixed with $0.3\ \text{m}^3$ of water at 60 °C. The final temperature of the mixture is
questions.explanation: By conservation of heat (same liquid): $T=\dfrac{0.1\times80+0.3\times60}{0.4}=\dfrac{26}{0.4}=65\ \text{°C}$.

questions.q: The spectral series of the hydrogen atom that lies in the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum
questions.explanation: The Balmer series (transitions to $n=2$) lies in the visible region of the hydrogen spectrum.

questions.q: A graph of pressure versus volume for an ideal gas for different processes is as shown [from a common point O, curve OA is a horizontal line (constant pressure), OD is a vertical line (constant volume), OB is a shallow curve, and OC is a steeper curve below OB, both ending at higher volumes]. In the graph curve OC represents
questions.explanation: For expansion from the same point, the adiabatic curve falls more steeply than the isothermal curve, so the steeper curve OC (below the isothermal OB) represents the adiabatic process.

questions.q: Which of the following statement does not hold good for thermal radiation ?
options: The frequency changes when it travels from one medium to another.
The speed changes when it travels from one medium to another.
They travel in straight line in a given medium.
The wavelength changes when it travels from one medium to another.
questions.explanation: When radiation passes from one medium to another, its frequency remains unchanged; only its speed and wavelength change, so statement (1) is false and hence the correct choice.

questions.q: A planet revolves round the Sun in an elliptical orbit [A and C are the ends of the major axis, with the Sun shown offset towards A; B and D are the ends of the minor axis]. The linear speed of the planet will be maximum at
questions.explanation: By Kepler's second law (conservation of angular momentum), the planet moves fastest at perihelion, the point closest to the Sun, which is A.

questions.q: Horizontal tube of non-uniform cross-section has radii of 0.1 m and 0.05 m respectively at M and N [a converging tube with a wide bore at M and narrow bore at N]. For a streamline flow of liquid the rate of liquid flow is
options: greater at M than at N
greater at N than at M
questions.explanation: By the equation of continuity, the volume flow rate $Av$ is constant along a streamline tube, so it is the same at M and N.

questions.q: A resistor and a capacitor are connected in series with an a.c. source. If the potential drop across the capacitor is 5 V and that across resistor is 12 V, the applied voltage is
The amount of heat energy radiated by a metal at temperature 'T' is 'E'. When the temperature is increased to 3T, energy radiated is
questions.explanation: By Stefan's law $E\propto T^4$, so at $3T$ the energy becomes $3^4E=81E$.

questions.q: The angle of minimum deviation for an incident light ray on an equilateral prism is equal to its refracting angle. The refractive index of its material is
questions.explanation: $n=\dfrac{\sin\left(\frac{A+\delta_m}{2}\right)}{\sin(A/2)}$; with $\delta_m=A=60\text{°}$, $n=\dfrac{\sin60\text{°}}{\sin30\text{°}}=2\cos30\text{°}=\sqrt{3}$.

questions.q: In the following combination of logic gates [(A): inputs 1,1 into a NAND gate, whose output feeds a NOT gate; the NOT gate's output combines with a third input line (0) into an OR gate; (B): inputs 0 and 1 each pass through their own NOT gate, and the two NOT outputs feed into a NAND gate; (C): inputs 1,1 into a NOR gate, whose output combines with a third input (1) into an AND gate], the outputs of A, B and C are respectively
questions.explanation: (A): NAND(1,1)=0, NOT(0)=1, then OR(1,0)=1. (B): NOT(0)=1, NOT(1)=0, then NAND(1,0)=1. (C): NOR(1,1)=0, then AND(0,1)=0. So the outputs are 1, 1, 0.

questions.q: A stationary point source of sound emits sound uniformly in all directions in a non-absorbing medium. Two points P and Q are at a distance of 4 m and 9 m respectively from the source. The ratio of amplitudes of the waves at P & Q is
questions.explanation: Since intensity $\propto 1/r^2$ and amplitude $\propto 1/r$, the ratio $A_P/A_Q = r_Q/r_P = 9/4$.

questions.q: A galvanometer of resistance $240\ \Omega$ allows only 4% of the main current after connecting a shunt resistance. The value of the shunt resistance is
questions.explanation: $I_gG=I_sS \Rightarrow 0.04I\times240=0.96I\times S \Rightarrow S=\dfrac{9.6}{0.96}=10\ \Omega$.

questions.q: The phenomena in which proton flips is
questions.explanation: In nuclear magnetic resonance, a proton's spin (magnetic moment) flips between energy states under a resonant RF field in an external magnetic field.

questions.q: $y = 3\sin\pi\left(\dfrac{t}{2}-\dfrac{x}{4}\right)$ represents an equation of a progressive wave, where 't' is in second and 'x' is in metre. The distance travelled by the wave in 5 seconds is
questions.explanation: Comparing with $y=A\sin(\omega t-kx)$: $\omega=\pi/2,\,k=\pi/4$, so $v=\omega/k=2\ \text{ms}^{-1}$; distance in 5 s $=2\times5=10$ m.

questions.q: According to the quark model, it is possible to build all the hadrons using
questions.explanation: Baryons are built from 3 quarks, antibaryons from 3 antiquarks, and mesons from a quark-antiquark pair, so 3 quarks and 3 antiquarks (of appropriate flavours) suffice to build all hadrons.

questions.q: An α-particle of mass $6.4\times10^{-27}$ kg and charge $3.2\times10^{-19}$ C is situated in a uniform electric field of $1.6\times10^{5}\ \text{Vm}^{-1}$. The velocity of the particle at the end of $2\times10^{-2}$ m path when it starts from rest is
questions.explanation: Work done $=qEd=3.2\times10^{-19}\times1.6\times10^5\times2\times10^{-2}=1.024\times10^{-15}$ J $=\tfrac{1}{2}mv^2 \Rightarrow v=\sqrt{2\times1.024\times10^{-15}/6.4\times10^{-27}}=4\sqrt{2}\times10^5\ \text{ms}^{-1}$.

questions.q: A cylindrical tube open at both the ends has a fundamental frequency of 390 Hz in air. If $1/4^{th}$ of the tube is immersed vertically in water the fundamental frequency of air column is
questions.explanation: Open-open tube: $f_0=v/2L=390$. With $1/4$ submerged, the remaining length $3L/4$ acts as a closed-open tube: $f'=v/4(3L/4)=v/3L=(2Lf_0)/3L=2f_0/3=260$ Hz.

questions.q: The surface temperature of the stars is determined using
questions.explanation: Wien's displacement law ($\lambda_m T = \text{constant}$) relates a star's peak emission wavelength to its surface temperature.

questions.q: [Circuit: a 12 V battery in series with a $6\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor, which is in series with a parallel combination of $4\ \mu\text{F}$ and $2\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitors, forming a closed loop.] The charge deposited on $4\ \mu\text{F}$ capacitor in the circuit is
questions.explanation: Parallel combination $=4+2=6\ \mu\text{F}$, in series with $6\ \mu\text{F}$ gives $C_{eq}=3\ \mu\text{F}$; total charge $=3\times12=36\ \mu\text{C}$, so voltage across the parallel pair $=36/6=6$ V, giving charge on $4\ \mu\text{F}$ $=4\times6=24\ \mu\text{C}$.

questions.q: A parallel beam of light is incident on a converging lens parallel to its principal axis. As one moves away from the lens on the other side of the principal axis, the intensity of light
questions.explanation: The parallel beam converges to the focal point where intensity is maximum, then diverges beyond it, so intensity first increases (up to the focus) then decreases.

questions.q: Continuous emission spectrum is produced by
questions.explanation: A hot solid filament (incandescent lamp) emits a continuous blackbody-like spectrum, unlike vapour lamps which give line spectra.

questions.q: A coil of 'n' number of turns is wound tightly in the form of a spiral with inner and outer radii 'a' and 'b' respectively. When a current of strength I is passed through the coil, the magnetic field at its centre is
questions.explanation: Treating the spiral as continuous turns $dN=\dfrac{n\,dr}{b-a}$ and integrating $dB=\dfrac{\mu_0 I\,dN}{2r}$ from $a$ to $b$ gives $B=\dfrac{\mu_0 nI}{2(b-a)}\ln\dfrac{b}{a}$.

questions.q: A ray of light is incident on a plane mirror at an angle of 60°. The angle of deviation produced by the mirror is
questions.explanation: Deviation by a plane mirror $=180\text{°}-2i=180\text{°}-2(60\text{°})=60\text{°}$.

questions.q: The electric potential at any point x, y, z in metres is given by $V = 3x^2$. The electric field at a point (2 m, 0, 1 m) is

Young's double slit experiment gives interference fringes of width 0.3 mm. A thin glass plate made of material of refractive index 1.5 is kept in the path of light from one of the slits, then the fringe width becomes
questions.explanation: Inserting a thin plate shifts the fringe pattern but does not change the fringe width, since $\beta=\lambda D/d$ is independent of the plate; so it remains 0.3 mm.

questions.q: Near a circular loop of conducting wire an electron moves along a straight line [passing below the loop, moving from right to left, as shown in the figure]. The direction of the induced current if any in the loop is
questions.explanation: As the electron approaches and then recedes from the loop, the flux through the loop first increases then decreases (and reverses as it passes), so by Lenz's law the induced current direction is variable.

questions.q: Hydrogen atom from excited state comes to the ground state by emitting a photon of wavelength λ. If R is the Rydberg constant, the principal quantum number 'n' of the excited state is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{1}{\lambda}=R\left(1-\dfrac{1}{n^2}\right) \Rightarrow n^2=\dfrac{\lambda R}{\lambda R-1} \Rightarrow n=\sqrt{\dfrac{\lambda R}{\lambda R-1}}$.

questions.q: The magnetic dipole moment of a current loop is independent of
options: magnetic field in which it is lying
questions.explanation: $m=NIA$ depends only on the loop's turns, area and current, not on any external magnetic field it is placed in.

questions.q: In ruby laser, the stimulated emission is due to transition from
options: any higher state to lower state
any higher state to ground state
metastable state to any lower state
questions.explanation: In a ruby laser, population inversion is built up in a metastable state, and stimulated emission occurs as electrons drop from this metastable state to the ground state, emitting coherent photons.

questions.q: A direct current I flows along the length of an infinitely long straight thin walled pipe, then the magnetic field
options: is zero only along the axis of the pipe
is zero at any point inside the pipe
is maximum at the centre and minimum at the edges
is uniform throughout the pipe but not zero
questions.explanation: By Ampere's law, a closed loop of radius $r$ inside the pipe encloses no current (all of it flows on the thin wall), so the magnetic field is zero everywhere inside.

questions.q: A convex lens made of glass has focal length 0.15 m in air. If the refractive index of glass is $3/2$ and that of water is $4/3$, the focal length of lens when immersed in water is
questions.explanation: In air, $\frac{1}{f}=(\frac{3}{2}-1)(\frac1{R_1}-\frac1{R_2})$; in water, relative index $=\frac{3/2}{4/3}=\frac98$, so $(\frac98-1)=\frac18$ replaces $\frac12$, giving $f_{water}=f_{air}\times\frac{1/2}{1/8}=0.15\times4=0.6$ m.

questions.q: Two sources are said to be coherent if they produce waves
options: having same shape of wave front
questions.explanation: Coherent sources emit waves of the same frequency that maintain a constant (time-independent) phase difference.

questions.q: Three resistors $1\ \Omega$, $2\ \Omega$, and $3\ \Omega$ are connected to form a triangle. Across $3\ \Omega$ resistor a 3 V battery is connected. The current through $3\ \Omega$ resistor is
questions.explanation: The battery's two terminals are the same two nodes across the $3\ \Omega$ resistor, so full 3 V appears directly across it: $I=V/R=3/3=1$ A (the $1\Omega+2\Omega$ series path is a separate parallel branch).

questions.q: In a common emitter amplifier the input signal is applied across
questions.explanation: In a CE amplifier, the input is applied across the base-emitter junction and the output is taken across collector-emitter.

questions.q: In a radioactive disintegration, the ratio of initial number of atoms to the number of atoms present at an instant of time equal to its mean life is
questions.explanation: At $t=\tau=1/\lambda$ (mean life), $N=N_0e^{-\lambda\tau}=N_0/e$, so $N_0/N=e$.

questions.q: A ray of light is incident on a surface of glass slab at an angle 45°. If the lateral shift produced per unit thickness is $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ m, the angle of refraction produced is
questions.explanation: Lateral shift per unit thickness $=\dfrac{\sin(i-r)}{\cos r}=\dfrac1{\sqrt3}$; expanding with $i=45\text{°}$ and solving gives $\tan r = 1-\sqrt{2/3}$, so $r=\tan^{-1}(1-\sqrt{2/3})$.

questions.q: Ferromagnetic materials used in a transformer must have
options: high permeability and low hysterisis loss
high permeability and high hysterisis loss
low permeability and low hysterisis loss
low permeability and high hysterisis loss
questions.explanation: A transformer core needs high permeability (to concentrate flux efficiently) and low hysteresis loss (to minimise energy dissipated as heat per cycle).

questions.q: According to Newton's Corpuscular Theory, the speed of light is
questions.explanation: Newton's corpuscular theory predicted that light travels faster in a denser medium (attraction of corpuscles), equivalently it is slower (lesser) in a rarer medium — a prediction later disproved experimentally.

questions.q: For the constructive interference the path difference between the two interfering waves must be equal to
questions.explanation: Constructive interference occurs when the path difference is an integral multiple of the wavelength, $n\lambda$.

questions.q: The accurate measurement of emf can be obtained using
questions.explanation: A potentiometer at balance draws no current from the cell, so it measures the true emf accurately, unlike a voltmeter which draws some current.

questions.q: The kinetic energy of an electron gets tripled, then the de-Broglie wavelength associated with it changes by a factor
questions.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
questions.explanation: $\lambda=\dfrac{h}{\sqrt{2mKE}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{KE}}$; tripling KE scales $\lambda$ by a factor $1/\sqrt3$.

questions.q: Which of the following is not a thermodynamic co-ordinate ?
questions.explanation: P, V and T are state variables (thermodynamic coordinates) describing the state of a gas; the gas constant R is a fixed constant, not a state variable.

questions.q: Two solid pieces, one of steel and the other of aluminium when immersed completely in water have equal weights. When the solid pieces are weighed in air
options: the weight of aluminium is half the weight of steel
questions.explanation: Equal apparent weight in water means $W_1\left(1-\dfrac{\rho_w}{\rho_1}\right)=W_2\left(1-\dfrac{\rho_w}{\rho_2}\right)$. Since steel's density $\rho_1$ is much greater than aluminium's $\rho_2$, the factor $\left(1-\rho_w/\rho_1\right)$ is larger for steel, so its true weight $W_1$ must be smaller to match; hence the aluminium piece weighs more in air.

questions.q: The amount of energy released when one microgram of matter is annihilated is
questions.explanation: Using $E=mc^2$ with the mass taken as $10^{-6}$ kg (1 mg, not 1 $\mu$g as literally worded) gives $E=10^{-6}\times(3\times10^8)^2=9\times10^{10}$ J $=0.25\times10^5$ kWh, matching option 4 exactly; the mismatch between the stated 'microgram' and the mass actually needed to reach this option is why KEA awarded a grace mark to all candidates for this question.
